response.content: Got it, will do. To continue where we left off: since you loved the bacalhau, you might also enjoy bacalhau à Brás, which is shredded cod mixed with eggs, onions, and crispy potato straws — quite different in texture from a baked version but just as beloved here. Bacalhau com natas is another classic, a creamy baked casserole with potato. Beyond cod, polvo à lagareiro (octopus roasted in olive oil and garlic, usually with smashed potatoes) is a Lisbon favorite, and arroz de marisco is a soupy, rich seafood rice worth trying if you like shellfish. For something heartier, cozido à Portuguesa is a boiled meat-and-vegetable stew, more common in cooler months. And of course, don't leave Lisbon without trying a proper pastel de nata — Manteigaria is a popular spot for a very good one. If you tell me what specifically you loved about the bacalhau, I can point you toward dishes or restaurants that hit that same note.
